subsystems.name: Semiconductor core
subsystems.role: the nanocrystal whose size sets the colour it emits — smaller dots emit bluer light.

subsystems.name: Shell
subsystems.role: a wider-bandgap coating that seals the surface and raises the fraction of absorbed energy re-emitted as light.

subsystems.name: Surface ligands
subsystems.role: molecules bound to the surface that keep dots separated and let them disperse in solvent, resin or ink.

subsystems.name: Encapsulation
subsystems.role: a barrier that keeps out oxygen and moisture, which otherwise dim the dots over time.

subsystems.name: Drive layer
subsystems.role: delivers the energy that excites the dots, either light or injected charge.
parts: electron and hole transport layers (electroluminescent type)

subsystems.name: Synthesis and purification line
subsystems.role: makes the dots at controlled size and washes them clean.

buildSteps.title: Pick the material system
buildSteps.detail: Cadmium-based cores give narrow, sharp colours but cadmium is restricted in some markets, so much work uses indium phosphide or perovskite cores instead.

buildSteps.title: Prepare precursors
buildSteps.detail: Metal and chalcogenide precursors are dissolved in a high-boiling solvent and kept under inert gas, because oxygen ruins the reaction.

buildSteps.title: Nucleate and grow
buildSteps.detail: In the hot-injection method established in 1993, precursors are injected into a hot solvent, causing a brief burst of nucleation followed by controlled growth. Reaction time and temperature set the final size, and therefore the colour.

buildSteps.title: Grow the shell
buildSteps.detail: More precursors are added to overcoat each core with a few atomic layers of a wider-bandgap semiconductor, which passivates surface defects and boosts brightness.

buildSteps.title: Purify and exchange ligands
buildSteps.detail: An antisolvent forces the dots out of solution so they can be centrifuged and washed; the original ligands are then swapped for ones suited to the resin or ink they will go into.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: For a display film, dots are dispersed in a polymer sheet and laminated between barrier layers; for electroluminescent devices they are printed as a thin layer inside a stack of transport and electrode layers.

buildSteps.title: Assemble into the device
buildSteps.detail: In a backlight film, a blue LED shines through the sheet and the dots convert part of that light to red and green. In an emissive display, charge is injected directly into the printed dot layer so it emits on its own.

buildSteps.title: Test and bin
buildSteps.detail: Each batch is measured for emission wavelength, colour purity and efficiency, and sorted for the wavelength range it lands in.

prerequisites.why: the ability to grow semiconductor crystals of uniform size in liquid is the foundation of the whole field.
blue LEDs or blue OLED pixels supply the short-wavelength light that dots down-convert to red and green.
dots degrade in air, so display lifetimes depend on keeping out oxygen and moisture.
indium phosphide alternatives emit broader colour and perovskites are less stable, so performance still trails cadmium.

prerequisites.tech: Printable charge-transport stacks for emitting dots
prerequisites.why: electroluminescent quantum-dot displays need stable transport and injection layers around the dot film.
synthesis and printing must be cheap and repeatable enough for large panels.

pathway.milestone: quantum-dot films in LCD backlights and emissive QD-OLED displays in shops
pathway.unlocks: wide-colour screens and a commercial base for making dots at scale.

pathway.milestone: printed, electroluminescent displays using cadmium-free dots
pathway.unlocks: thinner and more efficient panels made by inkjet printing rather than evaporation.

pathway.milestone: infrared dots in image sensors and photodetectors
pathway.unlocks: cheap short-wave-infrared sensing for cameras, phones and machine vision.

pathway.milestone: dots in photovoltaic and tandem solar cells
pathway.unlocks: tunable absorption that can capture parts of the spectrum today's cells miss.

pathway.milestone: dots as biological labels and light sources in medicine
pathway.unlocks: bright, stable fluorescent tags for imaging and diagnostics.
